idiom_name: hand-written class implementing the repository interface over HashMap
implementation_notes: Implement the port by hand in the test source set: a class that implements the same interface with a HashMap (or ConcurrentHashMap) as its store, so writes are visible to later reads. Mockito and similar libraries produce mocks and stubs configured with answers, so they are not the fake route; for persistence, an in-memory JDBC database (H2 or SQLite in memory) is the ready-made fake of the database collaborator and keeps the real SQL semantics. Create the fake per test or clear it in @BeforeEach so no state leaks, and keep an integration test against the real adapter.
pitfalls: A HashMap field on the test class, a static field or a singleton fake is reused across test methods and leaks writes - create it in setup and keep it per-test.
A Mockito double is easy to mistake for a fake: it returns defaults and asserts interactions, so tests written against it verify the wrong thing.
The fake must not narrow checked exceptions: declaring fewer than the real implementation makes the caller's catch blocks untestable.
